title: Deptford Emergency Help Points
summary: Emergency health facilities, hazard zones, and essential supply points for Deptford.
content: For life-threatening emergencies, call 999 immediately. 1. Nearest Hospitals with 24-Hour A&E: - University Hospital Lewisham (Lewisham High Street, London SE13 6LH). Directions from Deptford Station: ~30 min walk south along Deptford High Street, Lewisham Way, and Lewisham High Street (1.5 miles), or take bus 47 south directly down Lewisham High Street. - King's College Hospital (Denmark Hill, London SE5 9RS) — Designated Major Trauma Centre. Directions from Deptford Bridge DLR: ~40 min walk west via New Cross Road/Peckham Road, or take bus 436 direct to the hospital entrance (3.2 miles). 2. NHS Urgent Treatment Centres: - Lewisham Urgent Treatment Centre (located at University Hospital Lewisham, Lewisham High Street, SE13 6LH). Walk-in services for minor fractures, cuts, burns, and urgent illnesses. Follow the hospital route above. - Guy's Hospital Urgent Care Centre (Great Maze Pond, London SE1 9RT). Open daily 08:00–20:00 for minor non-life-threatening injuries. From Deptford Station: ~10 min train direct to London Bridge, or ~35 min walk west along Evelyn Street and Tooley Street. 3. Local Hazard Notes: Deptford Creek and the River Ravensbourne present tidal flood risks along Creek Road and Norman Road during extreme tidal surges or heavy rainfall. The Thames waterfront along Grove Street and Evelyn Street is also vulnerable to localized surface flooding. 4. Essential Supplies: Pharmacies and larger grocery stores along Deptford High Street and Evelyn Street supply bottled water, basic medicines, and first-aid equipment. Note: addresses and opening hours may have changed — confirm on arrival where possible.
